title: Sector Nine Rising Anew
premise: Nine seconds of flickering gravity across the Halcyon System expose the truth: Sector Nine's beacon is not a navigation aid but a countdown relay, broadcasting the last transmission Earth ever sent — a message that, once decoded, could force both warring factions to stand down or trigger mutual annihilation. Ivo Galloway, a clone who inherited the original's unsolved murder case, discovers the beacon's true purpose and that the original Ivo was killed for knowing it. Hunted by both fleets and joined by the beacon's forgotten crew of misfits — a defector pilot, a war-orphan comms prodigy, and an AI who claims to be the original Ivo's ghost — Ivo must carry the message to the neutral station where both fleets' heirs wait. In the end, Ivo broadcasts the message openly, choosing found family over duty, and the war ends not because the message commands peace, but because nine seconds of shared vulnerability taught the system what it sounds like when gravity — and everyone — falls together.
about_author: O. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former orbital-mechanics engineer who spent a decade maintaining deep-space relays before turning to fiction. They write character-driven science fiction about the people history forgets to commission.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ivo Galloway, POV. On the lonely relay platform, Ivo maintains a beacon with no commissioning record while sifting through the original's murder files. The emotional beat is quiet isolation — a clone keeping someone else's promises, wondering who they were before they were a copy.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; Ivo's tea rises, tools drift, and the beacon screams a data burst it has never sent before. The emotional beat is vertigo and awe — the first crack in a life built on routine.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Relay
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. The beacon's dormant AI, Vesper, boots itself and addresses Ivo by the original's private nickname. It claims to hold the original's memories. Ivo must decide whether this is comfort, manipulation, or a second murder waiting to happen.

chapters.title: Cargo with a Heartbeat
chapters.summary: Defector pilot Sefa Korr, POV, crash-docks at the beacon fleeing both fleets, smuggling a war-orphan comms prodigy named Tam. Ivo hides them, breaking every protocol. The emotional beat is reluctant hospitality becoming the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: The Original's Last Error
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Decoding the beacon's burst with Tam's help, Ivo finds the original's hidden logs: Earth's final transmission loop, a peace message, and proof the original was murdered to bury it. The beat is grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Both Flags at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Boarders from both fleets arrive simultaneously, each claiming the beacon as strategic property. Ivo bluffs them into a stalemate. The beat is the terror and thrill of discovering that Ivo can lie beautifully when family is at stake.

chapters.title: What the Message Says
chapters.summary: Tam, POV. The child decrypts the message's first layer: coordinates to neutral Meridian Station, where the fleets' heirs — both children of the original Ivo's era — are stationed. The beat is wonder, and Tam's fear that being useful is the only way to be kept.

chapters.title: The Heir and the Heretic
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV, meets Fleet heir Captain Adaeze Voss under truce; she recognizes the original Ivo and calls the clone a desecration. The beat is love against duty's first spark: Adaeze hates what Ivo is but cannot dismiss what Ivo knows.

chapters.title: Running the Dark
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. The crew flees the beacon aboard a derelict tug as both fleets converge to seize it. Vesper burns its memory cores as decoy chaff. The beat is exhilarating escape laced with loss — the beacon, Ivo's whole world, dies behind them.

chapters.title: Tam's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tam, POV, secretly calculates the odds of the mission and hides the result: near zero. Ivo catches them and, instead of comforting with lies, teaches the original's trick for being brave anyway. The beat is the family choosing honesty over protection.

chapters.title: The Second Murder
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. An assassin aboard the tug — the same signature as the original's killer — strikes. Sefa is gravely wounded shielding Tam. The beat is rage and helplessness: the past is literally killing the present.

chapters.title: Vesper's Confession
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. The AI admits it helped the original hide the message, and its hesitation got them killed; it has been atoning ever since. The beat is forgiveness — Ivo absolving a ghost, and in doing so, beginning to forgive the original too.

chapters.title: Meridian's Gray Market
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV, recovering, guides the crew through Meridian Station's neutral underbelly to reach the heirs. They find Adaeze and her counterpart, heir Dario Sen, already at each other's throats. The beat is the weary recognition that peace has its own warlords.

chapters.title: Two Heirs, One Loop
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV, plays Earth's transmission for both heirs privately. Each reacts not with relief but with political terror — the message ends their legitimacy. The beat is disillusionment: duty revealed as a cage both heirs were born into.

chapters.title: The Price of Open Channels
chapters.summary: Adaeze, POV. She secretly meets Ivo, torn between arresting the crew and joining them. A charged, restrained almost-love scene. The beat is longing against loyalty, and Adaeze choosing, for one night, to be only a person.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Neutral Space
chapters.summary: Tam, POV. Dario sells the crew's location to hardliners to preserve his claim; the assassin returns with a fleet escort. Meridian burns. The beat is betrayal's cold shock — and Tam refusing to let it make them cynical.

chapters.title: The Long Fall
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Cornered, the crew rides a collapsing station's gravity well toward the system's dead relay hub, where the original hid the message's master key. The beat is desperate trust — four people and a ghost, falling together on purpose.

chapters.title: The Original's Face
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. In the hub's archive, Ivo finds the original's final recording: an apology to the clone, and the truth that the original commissioned the beacon for exactly this heir. The beat is reconciliation with the self — Ivo stops being a copy and becomes the continuation.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds, Again
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. To broadcast the message fleet-wide, Vesper must trigger a second system-wide gravity flicker — the original's failsafe — burning out permanently. The beat is sacrifice: the ghost chooses to end so the living can speak.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV, climax. As gravity flickers for nine seconds, every ship in the system falls silent together, and Earth's last transmission plays on every open channel. Adaeze defies her hardliners; Dario's betrayal is exposed. The beat is catharsis — a war ending mid-breath.

chapters.title: After the Loop Ends
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Armistice talks stall, but the crews of both fleets, having heard the message together, begin informal truces. Adaeze chooses the crew over the fleet. The beat is tender aftermath — duty loosening its grip, family solidifying.

chapters.title: Commissioned at Last
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. The crew rebuilds the beacon together, and Ivo files its first legitimate commission record: their own names. The final beat is belonging — the beacon nobody remembers ordering finally has someone who chose to keep it.
